q: By June 30, 2027, a U.S.-North Korean summit takes place without South Korea having formally taken part in preparations for the talks, and the agreement from that summit contains no provisions on inter-Korean relations or on medium- and short-range missiles
basis: The forecast "No inter-Korean provisions in a U.S.-North Korean deal" is conditional on a summit without South Korea taking place, so a separate forecast asks the same question without that condition. Its 9 percent is the product of four estimates: that Trump and Kim meet by the end of June 2027 (35 percent); that, if they do, South Korea is not formally part of the preparations (about 85 percent: in all three meetings of 2018–19, Seoul was not a party to the U.S.-North Korean working-level talks, and in December 2023 North Korea defined inter-Korean ties as relations between two hostile states); that the meeting produces a written agreement (about 40 percent: of the three, only Singapore did, while Hanoi broke down and the Panmunjom meeting ended without a document); and that the agreement contains no provisions on inter-Korean relations or on medium- and short-range missiles (75 percent). The Singapore statement reaffirmed the April 2018 Panmunjom Declaration, so by this forecast's criteria it would count as including an inter-Korean provision; the 75 percent figure therefore rests not on precedent but on Pyongyang's current line of refusing to deal with Seoul.
rs: Announcements that a U.S.-North Korean summit will be held, the text of any agreement (as released by the White House or North Korea's Korean Central News Agency, KCNA), and South Korean or U.S. government statements on whether Seoul took part in preparing for the talks. A summit means the two leaders meet in person; an agreement means a joint document signed by both leaders or issued in identical text by both governments (a statement from one government alone does not count). Seoul's participation counts as formal if the South Korean or U.S. government announces that a South Korean government representative attended the U.S.-North Korean working-level talks as a party, or that a trilateral meeting of the United States and the two Koreas took place; prior consultation or intelligence sharing between Seoul and Washington, or mediation through special envoys, does not count. An agreement counts as including the relevant provisions if it mentions South Korea, inter-Korean relations or an inter-Korean accord (such as the Panmunjom Declaration), or if it addresses medium- or short-range missiles, or all ballistic missiles regardless of range. A reference to a "peace regime on the Korean Peninsula" or "denuclearization of the Korean Peninsula" alone does not count as an inter-Korean provision. If several summits are held before the deadline, the forecast resolves yes if any one of them meets all of these conditions. It resolves no if no summit is held or no agreement is issued.
